claims: NASA's Apollo 17 was the last human moon landing mission.
NASA's Apollo 17 landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley on December 11, 1972.
Astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days on the lunar surface.
Eugene Cernan was the final human to step off the lunar surface.
The crew of Apollo 17 was Eugene Cernan (Commander), Harrison Schmitt (Lunar Module Pilot), and Ronald Evans (Command Module Pilot).
Apollo 17 featured the longest total lunar roving vehicle distance.
Apollo 17 returned the largest amount of lunar samples.
Apollo 17 returned approx. 110 kg of lunar samples.
Apollo 17 was the first mission to include a trained scientist (geologist Harrison Schmitt).
Several uncrewed robotic probes have landed on the Moon since 1972.
Artemis II is the next crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
